text:
owen: Heads up — after the new kernel-chooser rollout we shipped last night, we're seeing a ~12% p95 latency regression on quantized models (INT4/INT8/FP8) for a subset of GA customers. Not universal but concentrated on long-seq workloads.
maya: which models / hw? can you paste the perf counters you saw? :thinking_face:
owen: mostly L2/L3 transformer stacks on H100 and MI300. Quick paste from the profiler for one affected route:
```
route: /generate/chat-longseq
model: red-model-x-8q
hw: h100-p4d
requests: 4.2k
seq_len_p50: 128, p95: 512
kernel_selector: seqbucket -> picked kernel_id=K_fp8_fuse_v2 for ~72% of tokens
latency breakdown (avg ms per token): kernel(K_fp8_fuse_v2)=0.48, kernel(K_int4_opt)=0.22, memcpy=0.03
fallbacks observed: when seq transitions from <64->>128 we hit an extra 0.14ms stall due to kernel rebind and KV cache reshard
```

owen: interestingly on MI300 same model mostly picks K_int8_tiled which is faster there, so selector misprediction across arch is the root cause.
tariq: sounds like our seq-length bucket boundaries are too coarse and we don't have per-arch confidence scores. two quick ideas:
- add per-arch kernel score matrix with decay + hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping mid-request
- introduce a tiny warmup path: for first N tokens after kernel flip, prefer conservative kernel that doesn't rebind KV layout
liam: +1. also we should instrument the selector to emit "picked_confidence" (0..1) and recent_win_count for that pick. if confidence < 0.6 and request has >1 seq-length transition, prefer safe fallback.
ana: small config prototype i ran locally (pseudo-yaml):
```
kernel_selector:
  strategy: sequence_bucketed
  buckets: [1, 8, 64, 256, 1024]
  per_arch:
    h100:
      prefer: [K_fp8_fuse_v2, K_int8_tiled]
      confidence_threshold: 0.65
      warmup_tokens: 4
    mi300:
      prefer: [K_int8_tiled, K_int4_vec]
      confidence_threshold: 0.6
      warmup_tokens: 2
  hysteresis: {flip_window: 3, min_dwell_ms: 12}
```

owen: that looks reasonable. two other datapoints from profiler-bot:
profiling-bot: ":bar_chart: quick summary for route /generate/chat-longseq (24h):
- 95th latency pre-rollout: 136ms
- 95th latency post-rollout: 153ms
- pct of traffic with cross-arch kernel mismatch: 8.4%
- median kernel switch cost (measured): 0.11ms (but correlated with KV rebind which adds 0.12-0.2ms)

link: https://perf.internal/flame/route-chat-longseq/1745 (internal)"

ana: another failure mode: our KV cache chunking layout is kernel-specific. switching kernel sometimes requires reshuffle of KV chunks, which triggers an async memcpy and briefly blocks scheduling. we should either a) avoid kernel picks that change chunking mid-request, or b) decouple chunking so kernel swap is a no-op.
tariq: decoupling is ideal but larger work. short term we can add a "chunk_compatible" flag to kernel profiles and prefer compatible kernels within the same request.
liam: for autotune sweep, recommend this plan:
1) run microbench per-arch per-bucket (buckets as above) measuring: exec_time, kv_reshuffle_cost, mem_bw_util, and pick_score
2) compute per-arch penalty = kv_reshuffle_cost * transition_probability
3) selector picks kernel minimizing expected_token_cost = exec_time + penalty
owen: can someone try a canary with config above + chunk_compatible constraint for 5% of traffic? also add telemetry for "kernel_switch_count" and "switch_cause" tags.
maya: i'll open a canary config and metric dashboard. tagging @tariq @liam for the selector changes.
ana: opened PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4207 (draft) — implements bucket boundaries + per-arch profiles + handler for warmup_tokens. includes metric emitters for picked_confidence and kernel_switch_count.
owen: action items:
- maya: canary rollout + dashboard (ETA 2h)
- tariq: implement chunk_compatible gating in selector (ETA today EOD)
- liam: run microbench sweep across h100/mi300 (ETA tomorrow)
- ana: follow up on PR and add unit tests for warmup behavior (ETA today)
- owen: prepare rollback plan to previous selector config if canary shows >5% regression
owen: thanks — let's keep thread for updates. :rocket:
